title: You don’t call Him Lord… until something inside you breaks.
paragraphs: You don’t call Him Lord… until something inside you breaks.

Not your image.
Not your reputation.
You.
Because deep down, you already know this:

You like Jesus as Savior…
but struggle with Him as Lord.

You want forgiveness.
But not surrender.

You want peace.
But not obedience.

You want heaven.
But still sit on the throne of your life.
And that’s the tension nobody posts about.

The quiet compromise.
The delayed obedience.
The “I’ll follow You… but not that far.”

A storm is raging.
Men who’ve lived on the sea their whole lives are panicking.

The storm didn’t recognize the disciples…
but it recognized its Creator.

The wind knew His voice.
The waves obeyed His authority.

We argue.
We delay.
We negotiate.

Some scholars interpret this moment not just as a miracle over nature,
but a revelation of identity.
Because in Scripture, only God commands the sea.

Psalm 107:29 says,
“He stilled the storm to a whisper; the waves of the sea were hushed.”
And now Jesus does the same thing.

So when we say “Jesus is Lord,”
we are not adding a title.
If He is not obeyed, He is not Lord in your life—only admired.

What is the one thing Jesus already told you to surrender—
but you’re still holding onto?

That relationship?
That habit?
That hidden sin nobody sees?

You pray.
You worship.
You show up.

But there’s a corner of your life where you whisper,
“Not here, Lord.”
That’s where the real storm is.
Partial surrender is still rebellion dressed as devotion.

The same Jesus who commands the storm
also calms the sinner.

You were not just drowning in waves—
you were drowning in sin.

Romans 3:23 says all have sinned.
Not some. All.
And sin doesn’t just make you weak.
But God didn’t leave you there.

Lived the life you couldn’t live.
Died the death you deserved.
On the cross, He didn’t just calm a storm—
Proving He is not just Lord over nature…
But Lord over sin, death, and eternity.
So now the call is clear:

You are not your struggle.
You are not your secret sin.
You are someone Jesus is calling out of the storm—into surrender.

Lay it down.
All of it.

Call Him Lord—not just with your lips,
but with your life.

Because one day, Philippians 2:11 says,
every tongue will confess Jesus is Lord.

Will it be worship…
or regret?
You’ll need it again when the storm comes back.
Next post… we’re going deeper into the one thing people keep hidden even after calling Him Lord.
